overview_description: Define custom components, then create and manage their objects, notes, activities, linked records and workflow status.
intro: A custom component is a record type you define, such as a service contract, whose objects belong to accounts and carry their own attributes, notes, activity log and workflow. This area has 39 endpoints covering component definitions, their instances (called objects on the `/components/{component_uuid}/objects` routes) and everything attached to an instance, and all seven SDKs call every one.
warning: **Replacing an object's linked accounts or orders unlinks every record you leave out, and changing its workflow status runs the transition and its actions at once.**
notes: **`component_uuid` takes two kinds of value.** Three instance calls take the component's dashed uuid: `POST /component/{component_uuid}`, and `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/component/{component_uuid}/{component_object_id}`. Every other call, including reading, updating and deleting a definition on `/component/{component_uuid}`, takes the definition's `cmp_` id.

**Instances have two sets of routes.** `/component/{component_uuid}/...` takes the dashed uuid and sends and returns the instance under the component's `name`, such as `service_contract`. `/components/{component_uuid}/objects/...` takes the `cmp_` id and uses `custom_component_object`, where `parents` names the record that owns the instance.
**Notes are sent as multipart forms, not JSON.** Put the text in the `note` field and any files beside it; a file's `uuid` in `attachments` is the `file_id` for the file calls.

**A custom object instance is created on the custom object's own path.** The create has no `instances` segment and sends `custom_object_instances`; the read, update and delete use `instances/{instance_id}`, and the update sends `custom_object_instance`.
**Listings page by cursor.** Records sit under `data`; pass `pagination.next_cursor` as `cursor` to read the next page, and stop when `pagination.has_more` is `false`.

endpoints.title: List component definitions
endpoints.summary: Returns one page of the custom component definitions.
endpoints.description: Lists the component definitions with each one's `cmp_` id, name, where it is used, its relation and its forms. Records are under `data` and paging details under `pagination`. Fields filter as `filter_<field>`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most records to return on one page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page, to read the page after it.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: A field to sort by, such as `created_on`, or `-created_on` for newest first.

200.description: One page of component definitions, under `data`.

endpoints.title: Retrieve a component definition
endpoints.summary: Returns one component definition, under `component`.
endpoints.description: Reads a single component definition by its `cmp_` id, with its forms and the attributes laid out in each column.

parameters.name: component_uuid
parameters.description: The component definition's `id`, which starts with `cmp_`.

endpoints.title: Create a component instance
endpoints.summary: Creates an instance of a component and returns it under the component's name.
endpoints.description: Creates a new instance of the component with this dashed `uuid`. The body has one key, the component's `name`, holding the instance's fields, such as `parents` naming the account that owns it. The new instance comes back under the same key.

parameters.name: component_uuid
parameters.description: The component's dashed `uuid`, not its `cmp_` id. It is the `uuid` the component has in the `GET /settings/components` listing.

schema.description: One key, the component's `name`, holding the instance's fields.

201.description: The new instance, under the component's `name`.

endpoints.title: Delete a component instance
endpoints.summary: Deletes a component instance and returns no body.
endpoints.description: Removes the instance with this `id` from the component with this dashed `uuid`. A successful call returns `204` with an empty body; reading or deleting the instance again returns `404`.

parameters.name: component_uuid
parameters.description: The component's dashed `uuid`, not its `cmp_` id. It is the `uuid` the component has in the `GET /settings/components` listing.

parameters.name: component_object_id
parameters.description: The component instance's `id`, as returned when it is created.

204.description: The instance is deleted. No body.

404.description: No instance has that `id`, for example because it is already deleted.

endpoints.title: Update a component instance
endpoints.summary: Changes a component instance and returns it under the component's name.
endpoints.description: Updates the instance with this `id` in the component with this dashed `uuid`. The body has one key, the component's `name`, holding the fields to change, such as `attributes`. The updated instance comes back under the same key with a new `version`. The shape of each `attributes` entry is not documented yet; the example sends an empty list.

parameters.name: component_uuid
parameters.description: The component's dashed `uuid`, not its `cmp_` id. It is the `uuid` the component has in the `GET /settings/components` listing.

parameters.name: component_object_id
parameters.description: The component instance's `id`, as returned when it is created.

schema.description: One key, the component's `name`, holding the fields to change.

202.description: The updated instance, under the component's `name`.

endpoints.title: Create a component object
endpoints.summary: Creates an object in a component and returns it, under `custom_component_object`.
endpoints.description: Creates a new object in the component with this `cmp_` id. Send its fields under `custom_component_object`; every key is optional, and `parents` names the record that owns it, such as an account. The new object comes back with its `id` and `activity_logs`.

parameters.name: component_uuid
parameters.description: The component definition's `id`, which starts with `cmp_`.

parents.description: The record that owns the object, such as an account.

endpoints.title: Update a component object
endpoints.summary: Changes a component object and returns it, under `custom_component_object`.
endpoints.description: Send the fields to change under `custom_component_object`, such as `attributes`. If you send `version_id`, it must match the object's current version. `code`, `parents` and `custom_form` cannot be changed and are refused. Each update raises the object's `version` by one. The shape of each `attributes` entry is not documented yet; the example sends an empty list.

parameters.name: component_uuid
parameters.description: The component definition's `id`, which starts with `cmp_`.

parameters.name: component_object_id
parameters.description: The component object's `id`, as returned when it is created or listed.

version_id.description: When sent, must match the object's current version.
